description: Set the value of thermal clump attributes. This is a synonym for the clump thermal initialize command. Individual attributes can be listed with the clump thermal list command, and all thermal clump attributes can be visualized.

python_sdk_alternative.workaround: itasca.clump.thermal.find(id) then set_temp()/set_expansion()/set_specific_heat()/set_power_app()/set_del_temp() per object - iterate for ranges

keywords.name: temperature-increment
keywords.description: temperature increment since last mechanical coupling

keywords.name: gradient
keywords.description: Apply a linear gradient in each of the axes directions starting at the origin; the stored value is the base value plus gradient dot position.

examples.description: Set the temperature of all thermal clumps
Base temperature plus a linear gradient from the origin (value = 100 + 2x + 3y)

notes: The 7.0/9.0 manuals attach a modifier block (add, gradient, gradient-x/y/z, multiply, replace) to every attribute. Read back live on 9.8 with 'ball thermal attribute temperature': 'add', 'multiply' and 'replace' go BEFORE the value ('temperature add 5'); 'gradient <v>' goes AFTER it. A trailing add/multiply/replace and the gradient-x/y/z spellings are rejected on 6.00, 7.00 and 9.8 (2D and 3D), after the plain value has been assigned. The 6.0 manual does not document the block, but 6.00 accepts 'gradient' all the same.
verification: Live-verified 2026-11-09 on PFC2D and PFC3D 6.00, 7.00 and 9.8 consoles (state grade): expansion, power-applied, specific-heat, temperature and temperature-increment each set and read back exactly via clump.thermal.* FISH intrinsics on all six consoles; gradient read back as base value plus gradient dot position (the clump at x=3 reads 13.0 after 'temperature 10 gradient (1,1)').
